hints.content:
The point $(-1,2)$ lies in the shaded area of one of the inequalities, and it is on the border of the shaded area of the other inequality.  

The graph shows a solid line for the border the point is on, so that border is included in the solution.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a graphed system of inequalities. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. There is a solid line representing an inequality that goes through the points negative two, four and two, negative four. The shaded region for the inequality is above the line. There is another solid line representing the second inequality that goes through the points zero, negative three and two, zero. The shaded region for this inequality is above the line. The point negative one, two is plotted on the line of the first inequality and inside the shaded region of the second inequality.

hints.content: Yes, $(-1,2)$ is a solution of the system of inequalities.
